title: Anaphylaxis & Adrenaline Auto-injectors
blurb: How to spot anaphylaxis, call 999 and help a guest use their adrenaline auto-injector.
siteNotes: Where the first aid kit is, and who the first aiders are.
What to say on the 999 call about where to send the ambulance, and who meets it at the entrance.
legalNotes: CHECK: the trainer says to give a second dose after 5 minutes if there is no improvement and another injector is available. This matches current Resuscitation Council UK and NHS guidance as far as known, but please confirm with your first aid trainer.

CHECK: the trainer says to lie the person down with legs raised, or sit up if struggling to breathe. Current first aid guidance varies on raising the legs; confirm the wording with your first aid provider.
Employers must provide adequate first aid (Health and Safety (First-Aid) Regulations 1981); not quoted on slides.

cards.title: Anaphylaxis & Adrenaline Auto-injectors
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- recognise the signs of anaphylaxis
- call 999 and say "anaphylaxis"
- help a person use their auto-injector and keep them safe

cards.title: The most severe allergic reaction
cards.body: Anaphylaxis is life-threatening and can develop within minutes. Getting allergens right prevents reactions, but everyone guest-facing should also know how to recognise and respond to one, because seconds count.

cards.title: Know what to look for
cards.body:
Look for swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat; difficulty breathing, wheezing or a hoarse voice; a widespread rash or hives; feeling faint, dizzy or suddenly very unwell; and collapse.

If a guest tells you they are having a reaction, believe them and act. Do not wait to "see how it goes".

cards.title: Call 999, then the injector
cards.body:
Call 999 immediately and say the word "anaphylaxis".

If the person has their own adrenaline auto-injector, such as an EpiPen, help them use it without delay. It is given firmly into the outer thigh, works through clothing, and is held in place for the required few seconds.

items.title: Believe
items.text: Take the guest at their word

items.title: Hold
items.text: In place for the required seconds

cards.title: If there is no improvement
cards.body:
A second dose can be given after 5 minutes if there is no improvement and another injector is available.

Fast action with adrenaline saves lives.

cards.title: Keep them still
cards.body:
Keep the person still. Lie them down with legs raised, or sit them up if they are struggling to breathe.

Do not stand them up or let them walk, as this can be dangerous. Stay with them until help arrives.

left.title: Do
items: Sit up if struggling to breathe

right.title: Do not
items: Wait to see how it goes

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Anaphylaxis is life-threatening and can develop within minutes.
- Believe a guest who says they are reacting, and act.
- Call 999 at once and say "anaphylaxis".
- Help them use their own auto-injector in the outer thigh, through clothing if needed.
- Do not stand them up or let them walk. Stay with them.

cards.q: Anaphylaxis is a life-threatening allergic reaction that can develop within minutes.
cards.why: It is the most severe kind of allergic reaction and can develop within minutes.

cards.q: Which of these is a sign of anaphylaxis?
options: A mild, brief cough at the table
Swelling of the lips or tongue
Feeling a little warm in the room
cards.why: Signs include swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat, difficulty breathing, a widespread rash, feeling faint, and collapse.

cards.q: If you suspect anaphylaxis you should…
options: Wait and see how they get on
Give them a glass of water
Ask them to go and lie down
cards.why: Call 999 immediately and say the word "anaphylaxis". Do not wait to see how it goes.

cards.q: An adrenaline auto-injector (EpiPen) is given into the…
cards.why: It is given firmly into the outer thigh and works through clothing.

cards.q: You should stand the person up and walk them around.
cards.why: Do not stand them up or let them walk, as this can be dangerous. Keep them still.

cards.q: A second dose can be given after 5 minutes if there is no improvement and another injector is available.
cards.why: A second dose can be given after 5 minutes if there is no improvement and another injector is available.

cards.q: A guest says they are having an allergic reaction. What should you do?
options: Ask them to wait a few minutes
Offer a drink and a seat in the lounge
Check the allergen file before doing anything
cards.why: Believe them and act. Do not wait to see how it goes.

cards.q: A person struggling to breathe is best positioned…
cards.why: Sit them up if they are struggling to breathe. Never stand them up or let them walk.
The injector is given into the outer thigh and works through clothing.

cards.q: Getting allergens right in the first place helps prevent anaphylaxis.
cards.why: Getting allergens right prevents reactions. Everyone guest-facing should still know how to respond.
